answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a time-locked stake that unlocks only after a history of verified useful work. New identities start at the nadir of trust, able to take only tiny tasks, while established agents ride the tide of accumulated reputation into larger jobs. A yarrow-like shared registry records each agent's completed work and slashing events, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred stakes and yields no shortcut past the slow trust ramp, making forgery far more expensive than honest participation.
